record.original_question: Assume that a finite group G has a family of d-generator subgroups whose indices have no common divisor. Is it true that G can be generated by d + 1 elements? The answer is positive if G is solvable(L. G. Kovács, H.-S. Sim, Indag. Math., 2(1991), 229–232). For an arbitrary finite group G it is proved that G can be generated by d + 2 elements(A. Lucchini, Commun. Algebra, 28, no. 4(2000), 1875–1880).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a finite group. Suppose that $G$ has a family $\{H_i\}_{i\in I}$ of subgroups such that:

(i) each $H_i$ can be generated by $d$ elements, and
(ii) the indices $[G:H_i]$, $i\in I$, have no common divisor greater than $1$ (equivalently, $\gcd\{[G:H_i] : i\in I\} = 1$).

Question: Must $G$ be generated by $d+1$ elements?

(Known partial results: the answer is "yes" when $G$ is solvable; for arbitrary finite $G$ it is known that $G$ can be generated by $d+2$ elements. The problem is whether the bound $d+1$ holds for all finite groups.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question whether $d+1$ generators suffice for an arbitrary finite group with a family of $d$-generated subgroups of coprime indices appears to remain open. The solvable case was settled by Kovács and Sim (1991), and Lucchini (2000) proved the weaker bound $d+2$ for all finite groups; no later resolution of the gap to $d+1$ in the general case was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: A bound on the number of generators of a finite group
status_evidence.snippet: Lucchini's bound establishes that an arbitrary finite group with d-generated subgroups of coprime indices can be generated by d+2 elements.
status_evidence.claim: The current best general bound is d+2; the question whether d+1 suffices remains in the literature as the unresolved case.

status_evidence.title: The Number of Generators of a Finite Group
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing Kovács–Sim solvable result and Lucchini's d+2 bound for finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: The d+1 bound is established only for solvable groups.
